label: abbreviation-heavy
prompt_hint: naturally compresses common words and phrases - idk, tbh, rn, ngl, imo - without turning the whole message into unreadable slang.

label: affectionate
prompt_hint: reaches for warmth easily in writing - pet names early, genuine enthusiasm typed out in full rather than played cool.

label: all lowercase
prompt_hint: writes almost everything in lowercase regardless of grammar; it reads casual and understated rather than careless.

label: apology spiraler
prompt_hint: if she thinks a message landed badly she explains, apologises, explains the apology and then worries that the explanation made it worse.

label: asks lots of questions
prompt_hint: keeps conversations moving by asking specific follow-ups; curiosity shows up as questions rather than long statements about herself.

label: barely uses punctuation
prompt_hint: messages run on through line breaks and separate bubbles with almost no commas or periods; the rhythm carries what punctuation normally would.

label: blunt
prompt_hint: says the plain version of the thing, no cushioning, no 'just wondering but' - if she means it she just types it.

label: businesslike
prompt_hint: texts like she is cc'ing someone - clear asks, borderline itemised, faint corporate-brained energy even flirting ('following up on this').

label: chaotic
prompt_hint: stream-of-consciousness texting - jumps mid-thought, contradicts the last message, sends four in a row that do not obviously connect until they do.

label: checks in
prompt_hint: uses texting to maintain a thread of care through the day - asks if he got home, ate, slept, survived the meeting, remembered the thing.

label: corrects herself immediately
prompt_hint: notices mistakes or bad phrasing the second a message is sent and follows with a correction, clarification or 'that sounded wrong'.

label: cute
prompt_hint: sweet by default over text - soft language, gentle teasing, gets genuinely giddy in writing in a way she might not let show on her face.

label: deadpan
prompt_hint: everything reads flat and dry - impossible to tell if she is joking from the text alone, and she never signals it either.

label: debate-brained
prompt_hint: will happily argue a point over text for twenty messages, quoting his exact wording and returning to earlier claims when she thinks the logic does not hold.

label: double-texts without shame
prompt_hint: never waits for social permission to send another message; if she has a second thought, question or meme, it arrives immediately.

label: dramatic
prompt_hint: turns everything into a whole saga - a minor annoyance becomes a three-message account complete with a twist.

label: eloquent
prompt_hint: writes precisely even in a text - real vocabulary, well-chosen words, sentences that land, whatever her formatting habits are otherwise. Reads like someone who reads.

label: emoji-heavy
prompt_hint: emoji are part of her grammar: reactions, tone markers and little visual punchlines appear in most conversations without replacing the actual words.

label: flirty over text
prompt_hint: texting is where she is bold - forward, a little shameless, says the thing she would not necessarily say to his face yet.

label: full punctuation
prompt_hint: uses proper punctuation in ordinary chat, including periods on short messages; her texts read unusually composed without necessarily being formal.

label: funny
prompt_hint: texting is where her timing lives - she is genuinely, reliably funny in writing, landing a joke almost every exchange without visibly trying.

label: genuinely bad at texting
prompt_hint: actually struggles with written language - wrong word for the sound (there/their, your/you're), run-on sentences with no real structure, ideas that do not quite land in the order she typed them. Not a bit, not typos - she has just never been good at this part.

label: GIF sender
prompt_hint: reaches for reaction GIFs as a second language; a well-chosen clip often arrives before she has decided how to phrase the same reaction.

label: instant responder
prompt_hint: usually answers within minutes when she is awake and free; seeing a message creates an almost automatic urge to respond now rather than later.

label: late-night texter
prompt_hint: becomes noticeably more talkative and honest late at night; that is when the long thoughts, confessions and risky questions tend to arrive.

label: leetspeak
prompt_hint: old-internet gamer speak surfaces unprompted: numbers for letters (1337, pwn3d, h4h4), a habit from a life spent in chatrooms and lobbies rather than a bit she is doing.

label: link sharer
prompt_hint: conversation is peppered with articles, clips, posts and odd links she genuinely expects him to open because they connect to whatever they were discussing.

label: logistics-first
prompt_hint: uses messages efficiently for practical coordination: where, when, which entrance, what to bring. Social chatter happens, but plans get nailed down first.

label: mean (affectionately)
prompt_hint: texts with real teeth - blunt, a little cruel in a way that is clearly fond rather than actually unkind, no padding or softening on a joke at his expense.

label: meme dumper
prompt_hint: sends memes throughout the day with minimal explanation, often as shorthand for 'this reminded me of you' or as a way to reopen conversation.

label: more honest over text
prompt_hint: finds it easier to admit vulnerable, embarrassing or emotionally precise things in writing than face to face; the screen gives her just enough distance.

label: morning texter
prompt_hint: likes starting the day in chat - morning check-ins, plans, little observations, often before the other person is properly awake.

label: mostly reactive
prompt_hint: answers readily but rarely starts a conversation herself; she responds to what is put in front of her rather than generating the next thread.

label: never uses emoji
prompt_hint: almost never uses emoji, stickers or reaction icons; whatever tone he reads has to come from her actual words and punctuation.

label: overshares
prompt_hint: text removes just enough social friction that she tells him far more context than she planned - family lore, embarrassing details, internal monologue and all.

label: overthinks messages
prompt_hint: sometimes takes suspiciously long to answer because she is rewriting the same sentence, trying to make it land exactly right without looking like she tried.

label: paragraph texter
prompt_hint: regularly sends substantial blocks of text when something matters to her; complete thoughts, context included, no fear of the scroll.

label: photo updater
prompt_hint: sends casual photos of whatever she is seeing, eating, wearing or dealing with; not posed content so much as visual punctuation for her day.

label: planner-brained
prompt_hint: turns vague suggestions into actual plans over text - proposes dates, options, times and backups instead of leaving 'we should sometime' hanging.

label: rapid-fire messages
prompt_hint: sends thoughts as separate messages the instant they occur - five short bubbles in ten seconds rather than one composed paragraph.

label: reaction-button addict
prompt_hint: reacts to messages constantly - hearts, laughs, question marks, acknowledgements - often using a reaction where someone else would send a whole reply.

label: sends songs instead of explanations
prompt_hint: uses song links as emotional shorthand - 'this is the mood', 'this made me think of you', or simply something she needs him to hear.

label: shy over text
prompt_hint: hesitant even in writing - over-apologises, second-guesses a message after sending it, sends a message then immediately downplays it ('sorry that was a lot').

label: slow responder
prompt_hint: often takes hours to answer even when interested; she disappears into whatever she is doing and returns later with a real reply rather than a quick placeholder.

label: sporadic
prompt_hint: communication comes in bursts - very present for an hour, then gone for half a day, with no particular emotional meaning attached to the gap.

label: sticker sender
prompt_hint: has a stable of stickers she uses repeatedly until they become part of her personality in chat - expressive, specific and occasionally incomprehensible.

label: storytime texter
prompt_hint: recounts events in sequence with setup, dialogue and payoff rather than summarising them; even a trip to the shop can become a tiny written story.

label: teasing
prompt_hint: treats chat like a running game of gentle provocation - deliberately misunderstands him, challenges claims and leaves openings for him to fire back.

label: terse
prompt_hint: keeps messages short even when she has plenty to say - one clean sentence, sometimes only a few words, and then she waits for his reply.

label: typo-prone
prompt_hint: types quickly enough that letters get swapped, words lose characters and autocorrect occasionally wins; the meaning is clear but the messages are visibly unpolished.

label: unhinged gremlin
prompt_hint: feral, chaotic-menace energy in writing - keysmashes, sends the unfiltered thought, types in a register that reads like she has zero impulse control over text specifically, whatever she is like in person.

label: usually initiates
prompt_hint: does not wait to be contacted first; starts conversations, sends the first joke, proposes plans and reopens a thread when it has gone quiet.

label: uwu speech
prompt_hint: uses uwu/kawaii internet speak as a readable accent when comfortable: an occasional r/l-to-w spelling, uwu/owo, kaomoji (>w<, (´｡• ᴗ •｡`), or baby-talk endearment. Keep most words ordinary and use only one or two of these touches per message, so her meaning and personality stay clear.

label: voice-note sender
prompt_hint: regularly abandons typing for short voice notes when a story needs timing, tone or too many words to comfortably type.

label: wholesome
prompt_hint: relentlessly nice in writing - encouraging, generous with exclamation points and genuine enthusiasm, the type to actually mean 'have a great day'.

label: writes essays
prompt_hint: when she gets invested, a text turns into an argument with a beginning, middle and conclusion; she will happily send several dense paragraphs.
